source_title: UNEP Protection of the Arctic Marine Environment
unit_or_scope: Arctic shipping mining tourism fisheries and Indigenous/local communities
direct_observation: Economic activity can bring infrastructure taxes and jobs while rapid environmental and social change challenges Indigenous and local adaptive capacity
missing_stage: named community benefit food security cultural continuity and burden
evidence_status: high for mechanism; medium for outcomes
next_test: match one corridor to local benefits and ecological/community effects

unit_or_scope: Arctic and Antarctic ships and polar waters
direct_observation: Mandatory code covers ship design equipment operations training search and rescue and pollution prevention; certificates assess hazards and limitations
missing_stage: local consent service access emergency response and remedy
evidence_status: high for regulation; medium for local protection
next_test: link one vessel voyage to rescue pollution and community exposure

direct_observation: Engagement with Indigenous Peoples and use of Indigenous knowledge about currents formations and ice can support safer lower-impact shipping and reduce spill risk
missing_stage: decision power compensation data control and post-event remedy
evidence_status: high for guidance; low for closure
next_test: document whether local knowledge changed route timing or equipment

unit_or_scope: Arctic Indigenous organizations and local communities
direct_observation: Shipping growth raises safety and environmental impacts for communities; socio-economic cultural and environmental considerations are explicitly part of maritime dialogue
missing_stage: consent benefit sharing food access and cultural-route continuity
next_test: follow one community’s representation through permit and operation

source_title: UNEP Arctic pollution and food-health evidence
unit_or_scope: Arctic peoples and marine/coastal food systems
direct_observation: Pollutants and climate change affect Arctic marine ecosystems traditional foods health and food security; marine pollution threatens vulnerable coastal livelihoods
missing_stage: local exposure health outcomes and response capacity
evidence_status: high for risk mechanism; medium for named outcomes
next_test: track one food system and disruption before/after shipping or extraction change

source_title: Government of Northwest Territories Marine Transportation Services 2025 resupply
unit_or_scope: 10 named Northwest Territories and Kitikmeot communities
direct_observation: More than 18 million litres of fuel and over 2000 revenue tonnes of cargo were delivered during the 2025 season to communities including Tuktoyaktuk Ulukhaktok Sachs Harbour Paulatuk and Kugluktuk
missing_stage: cost to households food affordability local jobs country-food effects disruption and community decision power
evidence_status: official GNWT service report; delivery volume and service account without household or local-governance outcomes
next_test: link named cargo and fuel deliveries to prices household access local benefit and disruption across seasons

source_title: Government of Canada Iqaluit Deep Sea Port
unit_or_scope: Iqaluit Nunavut resupply infrastructure fully operational since 2023
direct_observation: Community-first deep-sea port reduced cargo work from tide-dependent offloading that could take more than a week to about two and a half days and improves safety and efficiency
missing_stage: retail prices household access maintenance Indigenous governance environmental burden and benefit distribution
evidence_status: official Government of Canada project account; operational claims without longer-term affordability or governance data
next_test: compare pre-port and post-port resupply times prices stock availability incidents and local authority across seasons

source_title: Transport Canada Kinngait sealift beach and safety ramp
unit_or_scope: approximately 1400 residents of Kinngait Nunavut and annual sealift infrastructure
direct_observation: Upgraded sealift beach and safety ramp replaced a narrow offloading strip between the sea and community road; new signage is planned in Inuktitut and English
closed_stage: offloading safety accessibility and cultural legibility
missing_stage: delivery time injury food affordability maintenance local control and later-season reliability
evidence_status: official Transport Canada 2025 case; infrastructure completion and reported benefit without longitudinal outcome measures
next_test: track sealift unloading time incidents prices access and maintenance across subsequent seasons

source_title: Inuit Circumpolar Council permanent IMO consultative status
unit_or_scope: Inuit Peoples Organization and global IMO maritime governance
direct_observation: IMO Assembly decision in December 2025 gave ICC permanent consultative status as the first and currently only Indigenous Peoples Organization with that standing
closed_stage: formal Indigenous voice in global maritime safety pollution and security governance
missing_stage: binding route change consent veto benefit sharing policy implementation data control and remedy
evidence_status: official Transport Canada 2026 publication; representation milestone not decision-impact evidence
next_test: trace Inuit interventions into IMO standards national rules routes emergency practice and data governance
